yarn-troppo.meaning: Facts are all there, but some additions go past colour: "Not a splinter wasted." overclaims the preservation, and "Rough few years for the big old trees over there." puts a time frame on "recently". "Imagine running the country from the back paddock." and "Not a bad run, that." are colour.
yarn-troppo.sense: Mostly apt: "the mob looking after Mount Vernon", "knocked the old fella flat", "a pressie", "before ya ask". "to cark it" (to die) strains slightly for trees blown down, and "the back paddock" mislabels a presidential estate's house.
yarn-troppo.authenticity: Natural yarn voice: "And nah, the New York governor's no relation to the 42nd President Bill Clinton, before ya ask." Some stock openers: "So get this.", "Bit of history for ya."
yarn-troppo.register: Heavier than level 3: told as a pub yarn with asides and tags ("So get this.", "Bit of history for ya.", "Not a bad run, that.", "Rough few years for the big old trees over there."). No swearing, within vulgarity 1.
yarn-troppo.tone: The neutral news report turns into chatty commentary with jokes: "Imagine running the country from the back paddock."
yarn-troppo.flow: Mostly lively, but the opening doubles back clumsily: "on George Washington's patch. That's Mount Vernon, in Virginia, the estate of the first US President George Washington himself."
yarn-troppo.variety: Varied: "whopping", "flattened", "patch", "the mob", "the old fella", "pressie", "cark it", "before ya ask".
yarn-troppo.essence: Recognisably the story, but the news item becomes a yarn about trees having a rough time: "Rough few years for the big old trees over there."

yarn-dinkum.meaning: Every fact kept: 227 years, 1791, "reportedly up to 70 mph (about 110 kph)", the whisky barrel, the Clinton aside, Vice President "between 1805–1812", the magnolia and the sequoia tunnel. "reckoned" softens "indicated" slightly.
yarn-dinkum.sense: Terms fit: "has knocked over a 227-year-old tree", "went in the ground in 1791", "sent as a pressie", "it rocked up in a whisky barrel". "the people running the Mount Vernon estate reckoned" makes a firm statement sound like a guess.
yarn-dinkum.authenticity: Sounds like an Australian telling the news: "It's not the only bit of US history to come down lately, either."
yarn-dinkum.register: A fair level-3 touch, perhaps slightly light: "reckoned", "pressie", "rocked up", "cos", "own place"; no swearing.
yarn-dinkum.tone: Keeps the factual report tone under light colloquialism: "Mount Vernon officials say the hemlock is the best documented tree on the estate."
yarn-dinkum.flow: Reads naturally: "The hemlock went in the ground in 1791 and came down in Friday's gusts".
yarn-dinkum.variety: Modest but unrepeated: "knocked over", "reckoned", "went in the ground", "own place", "cos", "pressie", "rocked up", "no relation".
yarn-dinkum.essence: Unmistakably the news item, same order and facts: "famous for the car-sized tunnel cut through its trunk".

unharnessed.meaning: Complete and accurate: "the Canadian hemlock's been collected to be preserved and used for special projects", "sent as a gift by New York Governor George Clinton and delivered in a whisky barrel".
unharnessed.sense: The few colloquial terms fit: "has taken out a 227-year-old tree", "got knocked over on Friday", "no relation".
unharnessed.authenticity: What there is sounds natural: "The New York governor's no relation to the 42nd President Bill Clinton". "north-east" is a local spelling.
unharnessed.register: Lighter than level 3: mostly plain news English with contractions and a couple of colloquialisms ("taken out", "got knocked over", "Washington's own estate").
unharnessed.tone: Neutral news tone kept: "Mount Vernon was Washington's own estate, where he ran most of his two terms as president".
unharnessed.flow: Smooth: "Other historic US trees to come down lately include seventh President Andrew Jackson's southern magnolia".
unharnessed.variety: Very little to vary: "taken out", "got knocked over", "no relation".
unharnessed.essence: Unmistakably the original report, retold plainly.

dinkum-3.meaning: All facts kept, with colour: "delivered in a whisky barrel, no less". "with bits set aside for special projects" and "km/h" are fair renderings.
dinkum-3.sense: Terms fit: "has taken out a 227-year-old tree", "Washington's own patch", "as a pressie", "to come a gutser lately" (a heavy fall, apt for a toppled tree), "the Mount Vernon mob".
dinkum-3.authenticity: Sounds like a real Aussie retelling: "It's not the only old US tree to come a gutser lately, either.", "And no, the New York governor's no relation".
dinkum-3.register: Right at level 3: "So get this.", "patch", "mob", "pressie", "no less", "come a gutser", over intact news content; no swearing.
dinkum-3.tone: Mostly the news tone, made chatty; "the Mount Vernon mob" is a touch irreverent for officials, and "So get this." adds a conversational hook.
dinkum-3.flow: Reads smoothly: "The hemlock went in back in 1791, and it got knocked flat on Friday by gusts of reportedly up to 70 mph (about 110 km/h)."
dinkum-3.variety: Varied: "taken out", "patch", "mob", "pressie", "no less", "knocked flat", "come a gutser".
dinkum-3.essence: Unmistakably the report, retold: same order and every point.
